Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
The failing test `testElementDOM` calls the method `doTestElement` with the argument `DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM`. The `MODEL_DOM` constant is defined in the `org.apache.commons.jxpath.xml.DocumentContainer` class as `"DOM"`.

The current bug report describes an issue where an exception is thrown for attributes with namespaces, specifically mentioning the unknown namespace prefix `xsi`. This exception occurs in the `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMNodePointer.createAttribute` method when a namespace prefix is not recognized.

Looking at the `createAttribute` method, we see that it checks if the namespace prefix is not null and throws a `JXPathException` with the message "Unknown namespace prefix: \<prefix\>" if the namespace URI is null. This behavior aligns with the reported issue of unknown namespace prefix causing an exception.

Based on this information, the likely cause of the bug is that the method `createAttribute` in `DOMNodePointer` class is not properly handling undefined namespaces, leading to exceptions for attributes with unrecognized namespace prefixes.

Next, we will suggest the best locations to fix this issue.
```java
org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMNodePointer.createAttribute(org.apache.commons.jxpath.JXPathContext, org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.QName)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
